title: Annotatio IV §.XV: Fulbert of Chartres — mystery by SPIRIT OF FAITH; interior taste of bread of life
pass_a_gloss: His consensus with the truth is gathered clearly partly from the doctrine of his Teacher Fulbert, Bishop of Chartres, partly from Writings opposed to Berengar’s sentence and reviewing it. The Teacher’s doctrine shows itself clearly from his Epistle to Adeodatus, when among other things he writes thus: The mystery of faith is to be looked upon in the Eucharist not by bodily sight but by the SPIRIT OF FAITH; for what appears outwardly as the substance of bread and wine already becomes inwardly the Body and Blood of Christ; Not what is discerned by the mouth, but what is tasted by interior affection. Therefore exercise the palate of faith, dilate the jaws of hope, extend the bowels of charity and take the bread of life, the nourishment of the interior man. Again: From the faith of the interior man proceeds the savor of divine taste, while certainly through the infusion of the saving Eucharist Christ flows into the bowels of the one taking.
pass_b_english: Consensus with the truth is clear from his teacher Fulbert of Chartres and from writings that oppose and review his sentence.

Fulbert to Adeodatus: look on the Eucharist’s faith-mystery not with bodily sight but by the SPIRIT OF FAITH — outwardly bread and wine, inwardly Body and Blood; taste by interior affection; take the bread of life as the interior man’s food.
source_text: Consensus ejus cum veritate partim ex Præceptoris ejus Fulberti, Carnotensis Episcopi, doctrina, partim ex Scriptis, Berengarii sententiæ oppositis hancque recensentibus, liquidò colligitur. Præceptoris doctrina ex Epistola ejus ad Adeodatum se clarè prodit, quando is inter cætera ita scribit: Mysterium fidei non visu corporeo, sed SPIRITU FIDEI in Eucharistia intuendum, quod enim substantia panis & vini apparet exterius, jam Corpus & Sanguis Christi fit interiùs; Non quod ore discernitur, sed quod affectu interiore degustatur. Exere igitur palatum fidei, dilata fauces spei, viscera charitatis extende & sume panem vitæ, interioris hominis alimentum. Iterum: De fide interioris hominis procedit divini gustus saporis, dum certè per salutaris Eucharistiæ infusionem influit Christus in viscera sumentis.
